### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f148852752a2544bb25674cbc3385e279896e6c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `70ca97844e4c311bd1cdde714d67802d4d80c95e` — the merge of head `cbdd42efe6e144ff1fba17b11194b5f3815f3e6d` into base `f148852752a2544bb25674cbc3385e279896e6c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 70ca97844e4c311bd1cdde714d67802d4d80c95e && git checkout 70ca97844e4c311bd1cdde714d67802d4d80c95e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f148852752a2544bb25674cbc3385e279896e6c2 cbdd42efe6e144ff1fba17b11194b5f3815f3e6d && git checkout -B drift-repro f148852752a2544bb25674cbc3385e279896e6c2 && git merge --no-ff cbdd42efe6e144ff1fba17b11194b5f3815f3e6d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f148852752a2544bb25674cbc3385e279896e6c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f148852752a2544bb25674cbc3385e279896e6c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cbdd42efe6e144ff1fba17b11194b5f3815f3e6d`
Local-runs: none

PR #21270 (card #21110), isolated reviewer. Inputs: the card body and all six comments (triage 5927226845, claim 5942544148, reports 5943158706 and 5943617282, claim revision 5943184720, seat ACCEPT 5943656055), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` at the head (10 files, +450/-29), and the 46 check-runs on the head. Files at the head were read with `git show`; nothing was checked out, built or run. The Test Core shard logs were not readable through this session (the results store refused the download), so the check-run conclusions stand as the gate verdicts, as the brief says they do.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/types`: `ScheduledWorkPolicy` gains `readonly hostDisabledReason?: string`. An optional member on a published interface: every existing producer and reader compiles unchanged, and `resolveScheduledWorkPolicy()` never mints the key (pinned by key presence in `env.test.ts`). RIGHT, a widening.
2. `@objectstack/types`: new export `scheduledWorkDisabledReason(policy)`, reaching the package surface through `export * from './env.js'` (`src/index.ts:8`). Additive; this package has no api-surface snapshot, so nothing to regenerate. RIGHT, a widening.
3. `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`: `refuseScheduledWorkDisabled` gains a fourth REQUIRED parameter `policy`. Checked at the head: it is exported from `schedule-trigger.ts` but not re-exported by `src/index.ts`, and the package `exports` map exposes only `.` (dist/index), so no public signature narrows. Both in-package callers (`schedule-trigger.ts:700`, `time-relative-trigger.ts:331`) pass the very reading their gate refused on. RIGHT, internal.
4. `@objectstack/service-automation`: `policyDisabledFlows` moves from `Set` to `Map` of flow name to sentence. It is `private readonly`; all five uses at the head are Map-shaped (`get`/`set` at the gate, `delete` on pass-through at 3730 and in `unregisterFlow` at 4482, `get` in `describeUnboundReason` at 4578). The reason is read from the record, never re-derived (pinned). Not a public surface. RIGHT.
5. Wire shape of `GET /automation/_status` and `getTriggerBindingAudit()`: unchanged. `FlowRuntimeState.reason` stays an optional string; only its VALUE for a host-injected OFF moves from the deployment sentence to the host sentence. The runtime `_status` branch (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, the `_status` arm) returns `getFlowRuntimeStates()` verbatim, so the committed engine-row pins read the row the door serves. RIGHT, no accept-set change on any door.
6. The deployment path is byte-identical: the constant's value is untouched, `??` answers it whenever the key is absent, and the control pins (unset variable, no host policy) hold on the bind log, the audit and the status row. "No second copy" holds: the engine and both triggers no longer import the constant; the one remaining direct reader outside `env.ts` is `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` (the declarative `defineJob` gate behind the zero-argument switch read), where the deployment sentence is the true cause and a per-kernel policy never reaches. RIGHT.
7. Bind-log cadence: once per flow per distinct recorded sentence instead of once per flow, still at `info`. Benign, documented in the diff. RIGHT.
8. `@objectstack/spec`: `FlowRuntimeState.reason` TSDoc only; no key, type, export or `.describe()` moved. The `TypeScript Type Check` job (every spec gate, sequentially) is green, so no artifact went stale, and the doc pin in `automation-service.test.ts:452-458` still finds all four strings in the reworded block. RIGHT.
9. Landing shape: no governed path among the 10 files; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; head repo equals base repo; draft; auto-merge not armed; +450/-29, far under 5,000.
10. Check-runs on the head: the seven required contexts are all `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`). Every other run is `success` or an expected skip (`Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` on the two later `edited`/`labeled` re-fires). `Check Changeset` ran three times, all `success` (the third was still in progress on my first listing and completed green). No failure, no red.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/21110-scheduled-work-host-reason.md` grades `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/trigger-schedule` `minor`; its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and the PR body's line 2 carries the same line.
- This matches what the diff publishes: `types` widens a published interface and adds an export (at least `minor` under the widening rule); the two consumers change behaviour on their published `scheduledWorkPolicy` option and move `src/**`. No removal, rename, required member or public narrowing anywhere (①3 is internal), so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed, and no `major` is declared. RIGHT.
- `@objectstack/spec` carries no entry: its only change is a TSDoc comment. All four packages are members of the single `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json`, so spec versions with the group regardless, and the gate's level axis is PR-scoped (at least one moved package at `minor`+), satisfied by `types`. RIGHT.
- `skip-changeset` is correctly absent: three packages publish. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, round 0 (5943158706):
1. `time-relative-trigger.ts` one-line call-site edit outside the claim's named list: accepted as in-surface by claim revision 5943184720 and named in the PR body. Answered.
2. `trigger-schedule/README.md` per-kernel paragraph: accepted by the same revision; its three new sentences hold against `env.ts` (`??` on `hostDisabledReason`). Answered.
3. No door-level dogfood pin: verified that the `_status` handler adds nothing to the engine row, so the committed engine-row pins cover the door's content; the HTTP measurement was a scratch run, recorded in the PR body as evidence, not as a pin. Answered.
4. Spec TSDoc left incomplete: fixed at this head (round 1). Answered.
5. `minor` on all three packages: matches ②. Answered.
6. `origin/main` moved: now 10 commits past the merge-base, with an empty diffstat on every touched path and on `runtime/domains/automation.ts` and `runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`; the PR-event runs on the head ran against the merge ref. Answered.
7. Harness attribution: all four branch commits carry the model-free trailer pair; no model identifier in any commit, the PR body or the changeset. Answered.

Dev flags, round 1 (5943617282):
1. PR body patched by the seat, not the dev: the stored body names `automation-service.ts` as TSDoc-only cross-lane before the change list and ends in one session-URL footer. Answered.
2. No spec changeset: see ②. Answered.
3. No new spec pin: the existing doc pin covers the four kept strings; the changed sentence is prose. Answered.

`open_questions`: round 0 carried one (the spec TSDoc, A or B); answered A at this head. Round 1 carries none.

Seat acceptance note (5943656055), judged: `hostDisabledReason: ''` is asked to be a whole non-empty sentence and not enforced; `??` passes an empty string through, so a host that sets `''` would print a blank reason on all three surfaces. Not a failing finding: only host code sets the field (one consumer, cloud's free-plan policy; no metadata author reaches it), the PR body states both alternatives and why each is worse (a silent fallback restores the wrong-cause defect; a throw turns a reporting slip into a bind failure), and the row's shape is unchanged. Recorded as an accepted trade-off with reach limited to the host producer; a non-empty check, if ever wanted, belongs at that producer. Not escalated.

`out_of_scope_findings`: the `app-plugin.ts` `defineJob` gate (class none, reach none) is already recorded on the card body as #19834's open question 1 with "it is not filed"; the report's disposition matches the card. Not escalated.

Nothing escalated.
